name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Retinal Ghost Laminate
description:
The Retinal Ghost Laminate is a biochemically-bonded photoreceptor overlay applied directly to the surface of the cornea and retina via a controlled enzyme deposition process. A suspension of synthetic rhodopsin analogs and piezoelectric nanofilaments is introduced through a series of eye drops administered over seventy-two hours, during which the laminate self-assembles into a semi-permanent optical augmentation layer. Once cured, it interfaces with the user's existing visual cortex pathways without requiring surgical implantation, making it one of the few augmentations that leaves no hardware signature on standard bioscan sweeps.

What distinguishes the Retinal Ghost Laminate from competing optical augments is its passive persistence — the laminate requires no power draw, no wireless handshake, and no maintenance cycle. It operates entirely through biochemical signal transduction, translating photon input across an extended spectrum into neurochemical impulses the brain interprets as enhanced vision. Users gain low-light amplification, ultraviolet edge detection, and a subtle depth-contrast mode that makes structural outlines and silhouettes pop against cluttered backgrounds. The trade-off is that the laminate cannot be switched off; users must adapt to persistent enhanced perception, which causes disorientation in high-glare environments until neurological habituation sets in over several weeks.

The laminate was originally developed for deep-shaft agricultural inspectors working in bioluminescent fungal farms under Ironclad Agrisystems contract, where artificial lighting is minimal and UV markers are used to track crop health. It has since migrated heavily into the courier underground, the investigative journalism circuit, and among long-term squatters navigating unlit infrastructure corridors. Corporate security consultants prize it precisely because it evades augmentation disclosure laws — the laminate reads as a benign ocular treatment on most medical scanners.

cultural_context: The Ghost Laminate occupies an interesting social position in Meridian 88: it is technically a pharmaceutical product, sold through medical channels, yet its primary market is people who want augmented vision without the legal and social visibility that comes with declared cybernetic implants. In neighborhoods where augmentation disclosure is mandatory for building access or employment, Ghost Laminate users exist in a gray zone — technically compliant, practically enhanced. Among the investigative underground it has become something of a professional marker, a sign that someone takes their work seriously enough to modify themselves quietly. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals markets it through clinics under the brand name 'ClaroVite Ocular Therapy,' a naming choice considered cynically transparent by most who encounter it.
known_users: Undeclared augmentation users navigating compliance zones
Low-budget fixers who can't afford surgical optical implants
story_hooks: A batch of Ghost Laminate has been contaminated with an additional compound that records visual data to a remote Lazarus Pharmaceuticals server — users are unknowingly surveilled through their own eyes.

A character's Ghost Laminate has outlasted its rated lifespan and is beginning to degrade asymmetrically, causing one eye to perceive the UV spectrum while the other reverts to baseline — the resulting visual dissonance is becoming dangerous.

Someone is selling a counterfeit version of the laminate that provides the cosmetic eye appearance without the augmentation — targeting people who want to fake augment status in certain social circles where Ghost Laminate use is considered prestigious.
A witness to a corporate crime was wearing a Ghost Laminate during the incident — investigators need to find a way to extract the visual memory from the biochemical layer before it degrades.
